children: Working through this specific screen (Orders) has highlighted the importance of the need to implement our responsive type system.
There are a number of complexities co-exsisiting looking on the current screens, specifically form a rsponsive standpoint.
There are substatntial differences between desktop and mobile tablet and phone.
Information is hidden in the smaller devices such as the (Order Summaries). They only appear in desktop. When the breakpoint hits tablet the info disapears, leading me to question is it even relvant.
Then there is seemily alot of duplicated information, we could be cleaver and trim it where possible.

We Also need to think about the order of information, so for an example when I’m scrolling down the page lets say in desktop, the delivery information and tracking status sits above the Product image and it subset of product order details. In the context of desktop this is not too much of a problem as you are seeing all the information together as the screen can accomodate it.

The in mobile and tablet the infomation is still stacked in the same manner but becuase the product image is being scaled down to a size so small it becomes less clear as to which order it belongs to. Juts scroll up and down and you’ll see the iussue.
I think that in a narrow layout constraint, the image should come first, with the delivery status below it, with its subset of buttons.
It makes more sense visually as you see the image of what you ordered and then following that cue, you read the information associated with it. Makes much more sense and is far easier to process.
